title: Incident Bot v2 — PRD draft (Console deep links + on-call user stories)
linked_artifacts: Slack: #eng-oncall (what do we want in first 5 min context)
content:
Doc status: early PRD draft. This is intended to align Product (Console/Rollouts) with SRE + Platform on what “good” looks like for Incident Bot v2 and what Console deep links must do. Expect changes as we validate with on-call rotations.

1) Background / problem
Today, responders in #incidents and #eng-oncall lose time triangulating: (a) what changed (deploys), (b) what config changed (routing/flags/quotas), and (c) whether we are saturated (GPU/queues/KV cache). A recurring theme in postmortems is “we didn’t have the deploy/config context in the first 5 minutes,” which increases MTTR and increases the likelihood of incorrect mitigations (e.g., rolling back the wrong service or scaling the wrong region/pool).

Incident Bot v2 aims to standardize a consistent first-pass diagnostic package and make drill-down fast via high-quality deep links into Redwood Console dashboards/traces/rollouts.

2) Goals (product outcomes)
G1. Reduce time-to-triage for common incident classes by making “first 5 minutes” context consistent.
G2. Reduce time-to-mitigation by removing ad-hoc queries and providing direct drill-down links.
G3. Improve “graceful degradation” decisions during incidents by surfacing routing/fallback and saturation signals together.
G4. Improve reliability program KPIs: measured MTTR reductions and fewer repeat incidents due to missed context.

3) Non-goals
- Not a full incident management / paging workflow overhaul.
- Not replacing on-call judgment with automated RCA. The bot provides evidence, not conclusions (though we may add “likely causes” later).
- Not rebuilding the data warehouse or making Console the sole source of truth; links should land cleanly, but the bot can still render summarized context.

4) Target users / personas
P1. On-call engineer (primary): needs a fast snapshot + trusted links. Often operating under time pressure; prefers “what changed?” and “where to look next?”
P2. SRE incident commander: needs shared context for coordination, especially across multiple responders and time zones.
P3. Platform/control plane on-call: needs config diffs and routing/fallback visibility without risking tenant leakage.
P4. Support/CS liaison (secondary): wants tenant-safe summaries and links that can be shared internally without exposing secrets.

5) Key user stories (v2)
US1 — “Deploy correlation in 30 seconds”
As the on-call engineer, when an incident is declared in #incidents, I want the bot to automatically show recent deploys relevant to the impacted service/region so I can quickly confirm if a regression is plausible.
Acceptance notes:
- Show service name + version/image SHA + rollout phase (canary vs full) + timestamp.
- Include a single click-through to a Console “Deploy timeline” view, pre-filtered.
- Include links to GitHub PR(s) when available.

US2 — “Config diff without tenant risk”
As the platform on-call, I want to see a tenant-safe config diff (feature flags, routing policy, quota/rate limit, model pins) so I can confirm if a config push caused the incident, without exposing secrets or customer identifiers.
Acceptance notes:
- Bot output must be redacted; secrets and sensitive fields never appear in Slack.
- Provide an “expand diff” action that opens a Slack modal with safe pagination/truncation.
- Provide a deep link to Console “Config changes” that is gated by Console permissions and audit logged.

US3 — “Saturation snapshot + drill-down”
As the SRE IC, I want a short saturation summary (GPU util, queue depth, KV cache pressure, backpressure/admission control where applicable) so I can decide whether to shed load, scale, or reroute.
Acceptance notes:
- The bot highlights which signals are over threshold vs “normal,” with minimal noise.
- Each saturation section includes a deep link to the relevant dashboard and to the error budget burn view.

US4 — “Correct time window by default”
As any responder, I want every link to land on the right time window (e.g., last 30–60 min around incident start) to reduce confusion and avoid hunting.
Acceptance notes:
- Links should include incident start timestamp (or message timestamp) and a standard window.
- Provide “-15m / -60m / -6h” quick options via Slack actions (optional for beta).

US5 — “Works during partial outage”
As the on-call engineer, I want the bot to degrade gracefully if upstream systems are slow/unavailable, so I still get useful cached context and links.
Acceptance notes:
- If queries time out, show “cached snapshot at <time>” + links rather than blank cards.
- Show clear error states (permission missing vs timeout vs data unavailable).

6) Product requirements (what we are building)
6.1 Slack surface (Incident Bot v2)
- Context “cards” posted in-thread when a trigger occurs (incident created / command invoked / severity escalated).
- Three core cards for GA target:
  (A) Recent deploys
  (B) Config diffs (tenant-safe)
  (C) Saturation signals
- Interactive actions: open modal, expand details, copy command, open Console links.
- Reliability: must acknowledge Slack interactions within the SLA; bot should avoid slow synchronous calls.

6.2 Console deep link requirements (this PRD’s focus)
We need a consistent deep link contract so the bot can open the right Console view quickly and reliably.

Deep link principles:
- Deterministic landing: link should render a pre-filtered view (not a generic dashboard landing page).
- Stable parameters: avoid breaking links during Console navigation refactors.
- Safe by default: bot-generated links must not include raw tenant PII in query strings.
- Permission-aligned: Console enforces authorization; links do not grant access. If user lacks access, show a friendly “request access” / “break-glass” guidance.

Minimum deep link targets for GA:
DL1. Deploy timeline view
- Purpose: show last N deploy events for a service (and optionally region/pool), highlight canary/full rollout phases.
- Required params:
  - env=prod (default for #incidents)
  - service=<canonical-service-id>
  - region=<region-id> (optional; include when incident scope is regional)
  - start_ts=<unix ms>
  - end_ts=<unix ms>
  - incident_id=<id> (optional; for tracking attribution)
- Nice-to-have:
  - rollout_id=<id> when available
  - commit_sha=<sha>

DL2. Config changes / diff view
- Purpose: show relevant config changes for a scope (service/tenant/region) and provide a safe diff viewer.
- Required params:
  - env
  - scope_type=(service|tenant|global)
  - scope_id=<id> (tenant id should be a stable internal id; avoid customer name)
  - start_ts/end_ts
  - incident_id
- Security notes:
  - If scope_type=tenant, ensure the Console view never renders secrets by default; handle redaction consistently with bot redaction.
  - All accesses must be audit logged (Console side).

DL3. Saturation overview dashboard
- Purpose: single pane of glass for GPU util, queue depth, KV cache pressure, admission control/backpressure.
- Required params:
  - env
  - pool=<pool-id> (hosted shared pools OR dedicated pool id)
  - region
  - start_ts/end_ts
  - service (optional; for route/service breakdown)
- UX notes:
  - Default view should show both “now” and “trend over time” to support quick decisions.

DL4. Error budget burn / SLO view
- Purpose: contextualize severity and help choose mitigation urgency.
- Required params:
  - env
  - slo=<slo-id> OR (service + route)
  - region
  - start_ts/end_ts

DL5. Trace/log correlation shortcuts
- Purpose: jump straight to traces/logs filtered to service + region + time window.
- Required params:
  - env
  - service
  - region
  - start_ts/end_ts
- Note: trace sampling and indexing delays mean we should message “may take a few minutes to populate” in some cases.

Link formatting / “contract” (proposal)
- Standard base path: https://console.redwoodinference.com/<view>?<params>
- Params must be URL-safe, and incident_id should be a non-guessable internal id (or Slack thread timestamp) used for analytics attribution.
- Time window default: [incident_start_ts - 30m, incident_start_ts + 30m] for most views; for deploy timeline, widen to 2–6 hours depending on deploy cadence.
- If bot doesn’t know incident_start_ts, use message timestamp.

6.3 Measurement + analytics requirements
We want to measure whether the bot + links actually reduce time and improve decisions.

Event instrumentation (beta scope):
- bot_context_posted (includes which cards succeeded/failed)
- bot_link_clicked (with link_type, view, incident_id, user_role if available)
- bot_modal_opened (diff expanded, saturation expanded)
- console_view_loaded_from_bot (Console receives incident_id/link_type params)

Context completeness score (draft)
- 0–3 score for presence of: deploy card, config card, saturation card.
- Track per incident and per severity.
- Track “degraded mode” events separately (timeouts, cached-only).

7) Success metrics (tied to reliability program KPIs)
Primary (program-level):
- MTTR reduction for target incident classes (deploy regressions, misconfig pushes, regional saturation).
  - Proposed target: 15–25% MTTR reduction in the first 1–2 quarters after GA, measured vs baseline.
- Time-to-triage reduction (time from incident declared to first confirmed hypothesis / mitigation attempt).

Secondary (product adoption/quality):
- Adoption: % of incidents where responders interact with at least one bot card or click at least one deep link.
- Context completeness: average score and distribution; target >85% incidents have all three cards (or a clear reason why not).
- Link quality: % of bot links that lead to a filtered view without manual re-filtering (measured via Console “refine filters” events, or survey).
- Bot performance: P95 time-to-first-card and P95 time-to-complete-context; error rates; number of timeouts.

Guardrail metrics (avoid making incidents worse):
- Telemetry query cost/cadence: ensure bot-driven queries don’t cause measurable load spikes.
- Noise: count of cards posted per incident thread; aim for concise summaries with optional drill-down.
- Security: 0 incidents of secret/PII leakage via Slack output.

8) Rollout plan (product + comms)
- Beta cohort: SRE rotation only (limited regions/services) behind feature flag.
- Expand to platform and core product on-calls once:
  - redaction tests pass,
  - audit logging verified,
  - query budgets/caching in place,
  - Console links validated for all target views.
- GA: announce in #announcements and update on-call playbooks/runbooks.

9) Dependencies / cross-team asks
- SRE: baseline MTTR + incident class taxonomy; define incident_id; feedback loop.
- Platform: config diff endpoint + permissioning + break-glass story.
- Release Eng: deploy metadata export + joining to service registry.
- Telemetry: saturation metrics standardization + dashboard endpoints.
- Console team: implement deep link targets and ensure stable query param contract.

10) Open questions / TODOs
- Console deep link ownership: who guarantees backward compatibility for URL contracts? (Proposal: Console team + a lightweight “link contract” test suite.)
- Tenant identifiers: what is the safest stable identifier for bot links? (Prefer internal tenant UUID; never customer name.)
- Default time windows per link type: do we standardize globally or tailor by incident type?
- “Expand diff” access: should Slack modal display be more restrictive than Console? (Current inclination: Slack is always redacted; Console shows more details only with proper role.)
- Should we show recommended mitigations (e.g., “consider reroute”) in v2, or keep it evidence-only until we trust the signals?

11) Notes from early feedback (as of last edit)
- On-call feedback: cards must be short; long diffs should be opt-in via modal.
- SRE feedback: a single “SLO burn link” per region/service is frequently more actionable than many metrics.
- Console ask: links must land with correct filters and should render fast on mobile (many responders triage from phones).

Appendix: proposed “definition of done” for deep links
- For each DL target, we have:
  - documented params and defaults,
  - at least one automated test ensuring the view loads with params,
  - a fallback behavior if params are missing/invalid (don’t 404; show a friendly message and a default view),
  - analytics events for attribution.

End of draft.
